messages:
alyssa (infosec): Heads up — during the RBAC role->policy refactor I noticed an active session in the private control plane that still had `org:admin` perms even though the binding was removed last night. Not sure if this is session caching or a token scope bug.

mike (platform): :eyes: do you have the session id or a sample user?

alyssa (infosec): user=rachel@redwood.test, session_id=3f9b2a7c. Audit log shows grant at 2239799000 and the binding deletion at 2239799500. User actions at 2239799800 still succeeded for admin-only endpoints.

rachel (privinfra): I did some deploys while debugging; that session was from my laptop. I can repro if it helps.

sam (sre): Quick hypothesis: we changed role name and left session TTL able to reference cached role ids. The runtime reads role mapping on auth only at session create, not on subsequent requests. If the role renaming left an alias, old session keeps old privileges.

alyssa (infosec): Agreed — looks like session-store has role_id and a copy of permissions. After refactor the role id -> policy mapping changed. We should treat role->policy mapping as canonical and invalidate sessions on RBAC canonical changes.

mike (platform): For immediate mitigation: revoke sessions for affected users and rotate the private control plane service tokens for the short term. I can push a cron to expire sessions with role_id=X.

rachel (privinfra): How can I find all sessions mapped to that role id?

mike (platform): Run this against the session db (postgres):

```sql
SELECT id, user_email, created_at, role_id FROM sessions WHERE role_id = 'role_42_oldname';
-- then
DELETE FROM sessions WHERE role_id = 'role_42_oldname';
```

sam (sre): Also grep audit logs to ensure nothing escalated beyond scope. Example: `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name="priv-controlplane" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Admin"' --limit 50`

alyssa (infosec): I ran an audit query and found 8 admin-only actions between binding deletion and session expiry. No data exfil patterns, mostly debug endpoints. Still want a short incident ticket.

mike (platform): I'll prepare a hotfix: on RBAC binding changes we publish a "rbac.change" event to the sessions service that triggers invalidation for impacted role_ids. Patch + DB cleanup now, and followup to make session validation reference live role->policy mapping when evaluating sensitive endpoints.

rachel (privinfra): Thanks — pls also ensure this triggers for private control plane only (we don't want noisy invalidations for hosted ephemeral sessions).

mike (platform): good point. we'll scope by deployment_type = 'private' or 'dedicated' when invalidating.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: platform/session-invalidate-handler@hotfix-22398 -> staging (started) :rocket:

sam (sre): Postmortem items: 1) emit rbac.change events; 2) add session role TTL and on-change invalidation; 3) add audit alert for simultaneous role binding delete + admin ops; 4) update runbook for private control plane RBAC refactors.

alyssa (infosec): I've opened INC-22398 and assigned owners. Will add timeline and evidence. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
